tasks.title: VO drift from an altitude error
tasks.statement: A nadir camera, with the frame scale taken from AGL. The height above ground is overestimated by **{e} %**, and the vehicle flew **{d} m** in a straight line. Find the position error of pure visual odometry due to scale (m).
tasks.solution: The shift in meters = the shift in pixels · AGL / f, so the relative altitude error carries over entirely into the path length: Δ = D · e/100. 5 % over 1000 m is 50 m on a straight line. On a closed route the scale error partly cancels: in the lab, 20.8 m at 1000 m and 10.9 m at 1500 m.

tasks.title: How many RANSAC iterations a homography needs
tasks.statement: After the ratio test, the inlier ratio is **{w}**. A homography needs 4 point pairs per hypothesis. How many RANSAC iterations give a 0.99 probability of drawing four correct pairs at least once? The formula is N = ln(1 − p) / ln(1 − w⁴).
tasks.solution: The probability that all 4 pairs are correct is w⁴; N = ln(0.01)/ln(1 − w⁴). At w = 0.5 that is 72 iterations, at w = 0.2 about 2900: a change of season that halves the inlier ratio makes RANSAC tens of times more expensive. Hence a strict ratio test and a search window from the position prediction.

tasks.title: How often you need map fixes
tasks.statement: Between fixes the position is carried by VO with a drift of **{k} %** of the path. The speed is **{v} m/s**, and the allowed error before the next fix is **{E} m**. Find the maximum interval between successful fixes (s).
tasks.solution: The error grows as k/100 · v · t, so t = E / (k/100 · v). At 3 %, 15 m/s and 15 m that is 33 s, or 500 m of path: a stretch without landmarks (water, a flat field) longer than this cannot be crossed within tolerance.

tasks.title: Minimum frame rate for VO
tasks.statement: A nadir camera: focal length 500 px, 480 px along the flight direction. Altitude **{h} m**, speed **{v} m/s**. For stable VO, consecutive frames must overlap by at least 60 %. Find the minimum frame rate (Hz).
tasks.solution: The frame footprint along the flight direction is L = 480 · h / 500 = 0.96 · h. The shift between frames is at most 40 % of the footprint: v / fps ≤ 0.4 · L, hence fps ≥ v / (0.384 · h). At 100 m and 10 m/s that is 0.26 Hz (2 Hz in the lab, 95 % overlap); at 30 m and 25 m/s it is already 2.2 Hz.
